column8: Thu 19 Nov: evidence for 3d's half-clause (money voted each year, card Q9c): Hsinchu paid its operator in half-year lots in 2019-2020. Store, or one clause beside row 2. The half-year split may just be procurement practice (an expansion option), so never say the city doubted its operator.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d's half-clause, the plainest local proof that renewal is not a promise. Rater read pcc.mlwmlw.org today: the 2025 contract (NT$4.0m) was awarded 31 Dec 2024 and the 2026 one (NT$5.4m) on 6 Jan 2026, both to 智邦藝術基金會. Say awarded, not signed: the signing date is not shown. 3d takes no number.

Thu 19 Nov: store only. The contract was about three-quarters of the foundation's whole spending (checked). But only about NT$1.4m a year is its own goes too far: the rest of its spending need not be the village's or the company's money. Give the contract's share only.
Thu 19 Nov: store only, for 3.0's a base, not the whole budget: a busy public village ran on about four shared staff. The count may leave out front-desk staff paid inside the contract.
Thu 19 Nov: store only. A yardstick for what a year of running money buys: 19 shows, 31,212 visits, about NT$128 a visit (checked). Not material for the investment case.
Thu 19 Nov: store only. The artist-facing price list: NT$155,000 a resident, about $4,730 at 32.768 (checked). Read from a copy on Taitung's site, so cite Hsinchu's own call if used.

Thu 19 Nov: 3.0 background (Q9c-017 already says people are most of the cost). NT$310,000 is 5.7% of the 2026 contract, 7.8% of 2025's and about 19% of one payment (checked). Short stays and exchanges may also sit inside the contract.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e or 3a background. Under 閉館不閉村 the city paid over NT$25m for the roof while the operator's yearly money ran on: the same split as the plan's ten payments and the facility. A real public event; store or one clause.
Thu 19 Nov: store only. Refines Q9c-026: only Hsinchu never stopped, on the city's own word.

Thu 19 Nov: sizing for 3a or 3.0. Upkeep alone ran NT$0.82m-1.54m a year, 50-94% of one payment (the deficit matches to the dollar, checked). These buildings are not confirmed as the village's, so call it a public heritage site, not an artist village.
Thu 19 Nov: store only. One site that is free to use by design; Taipei Artist Village earned about 29% of its 2018 budget (Q9-032), so never generalise earned income as nil.

Thu 19 Nov: the lower bound behind claim 2: NT$1.10m a year (NT$2.81m over about 2.56 years), about $33,500, so one payment is about 1.5 times it (checked). Also a counterexample to one year at a time. F3 was partly idle (Q49-037), so a low contract may mean low activity.
Thu 19 Nov: store only. The contract period is not shown, it includes opening events, and a craft village may not be a residency. Do not use it as a yearly benchmark until both are read.
Thu 19 Nov: store only, background for 3a: a city residency hides its staff in the city payroll, while a founder's residency pays them from its running money. Interview, not accounts.
Thu 19 Nov: store only. Prices one Soulangh resident at NT$240,000, about $7,324; one payment buys about 6.8 (checked). The NT$800 re-split is Keel's inference. Leaves out staff, building and travel.

Thu 19 Nov: twin of Q10d-009 and NUMBERS 8d: each 2026 village grant was NT$0.7m-1.8m, $21,362-$54,932, and Q9c-035 already says a payment is about one village grant. Adds Soulangh's NT$2.1m for 2022 (78-91%, checked). That grant comes on top of the city's own budget.

Thu 19 Nov: twin of Q11d-003 (public money arrives after the work, Laura's cash first) and Q48-012 (money only after the council passes the budget). Adds Kinmen and Soulangh, but these are artist stipends, not running money.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d background, with Q55-009 (cut pro rata after the budget review): a 25-year-old space's operating grant fell 23% in one year, NT$650,000 to NT$500,000 (checked). No reason is given, so never tie it to a recession or to markets.
Thu 19 Nov: twin of Q10d-018, the calendar-year operating grant (Q10d-019 is already merged there). Adds 2024: 20 groups, NT$12m, mean NT$600,000 (checked).

Thu 19 Nov: twin of Q142-030 (NCAF lives on its fund's returns); adds 2025, when investment income was 65.6% of income (checked). Its use line is wrong: in 2015 NCAF's income fell but its grants rose (Q4b-027). Say its income, not its grants, rides on markets.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e evidence that the site is a residency's weak link: the lease was not renewed in 2018, and the landlord's own space opened on the site. Largely the space's own account, in a student paper.
Thu 19 Nov: store only. It is not shown that the 2026 空場 grantee is the same group, so do not say the people outlasted the lease until it is.
Thu 19 Nov: store only, beside row 21 for 3e: site terms are short (one year at most at Board 435 and Treasure Hill's micro-settlement in 2018). A 2018 picture; row 24 shows a later change.
Thu 19 Nov: store only. An artist's studio term is not a funder's term, so never set Board 435's three years against Laura's ten. Sources conflict on when the term changed.
Thu 19 Nov: store only. Operators change with the contract cycle (with Q9c-025), so Hsinchu's decade with one operator is unusual. One case.
Thu 19 Nov: twin of Q9c-004 (bodies funded three years running must file a self-improvement plan); adds the 2027 round's dates, 16 Nov-15 Dec 2026.

Thu 19 Nov: the rate is in conflict, not settled. The CBC's daily page (rater read it today, dated 12 Nov 2026) gives the same five banks' one-year fixed rate as 0.77% (Q69-034 saw it too), against the 1.70% posted rate. The lower figure is likely the large-deposit rate a NT$30m fund would get. Give both, each with its basis.

Thu 19 Nov: a 3a or 3d store line; the arithmetic checks (NT$1,638,400 / 1.70% = NT$96.4m, about $2.94m at 32.768). At the CBC page's 0.77% (row 27) it is about NT$213m, so give the rate's basis or say more than NT$96m. It sets ten payments beside a fund kept forever, so never imply her gift is worth such a fund. 3d's half-clause takes no number.

Thu 19 Nov: store only, with Q48-040 and Q100-035: local culture foundations need NT$3m-10m, which earns NT$51,000-170,000 a year at 1.70% and less at the large-deposit rate (row 27). Either way it pays almost nothing.

Thu 19 Nov: store only, beside Q100-009 (Chimei's permanent fund) and Q83-024: Taiwan locks a foundation's fund by law, while Laura's reserve pays out its principal on dated schedule. Never call the reserve an endowment.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d background, stronger than its twin Q48-041 for the 5% cap on shares. Drop will read (no co-sponsor was asked); say the rule lists deposits and government bonds first. It is one city's rule for a foundation's own fund, so set it beside the reserve only: her half kept holds world shares.
Thu 19 Nov: twin of Q11d-014, the national Foundations Act's 10% cap on any one grantee with the same exceptions; Taichung only repeats it.

Thu 19 Nov: sizing for 3a or 3.0: Paul Chiang's operator spends about NT$5.6m a year (NT$4.2m in nine months, checked), close to Hsinchu's NT$5.4m. This is the operator's spending only; the foundation's own budget is unread. USI's NT$3m is a co-sponsor's gift, not the founder's.
Thu 19 Nov: twin of Q11e-005 (Paul Chiang's 2025 report gives no money figures). Adds 76 volunteers and visit counts; store only.
Thu 19 Nov: store only. One exchange show's budget (NT$5.4m) equalled a year of Hsinchu's running money; the award amount is not read.

Thu 19 Nov: sizes 3.0 and 3a's a base, not its whole budget (H9-119) in Taiwan: about 1.5 times the smallest village contract and 30-41% of Hsinchu's (every ratio checked at 32.768). Drop one or two staff: a Treasure Hill staff-year is about NT$730,000 (Q102-033) and upkeep alone is NT$0.82m-1.54m. For Hsinchu say two and a half to three times, not about three. Never say it covers the residency.

Thu 19 Nov: twin of Q9c-014 (the money inside is voted yearly), with Q9c-001 and H9-116. The rewritten claim 1 holds, but its exceptions leave out Treasure Hill's three-year administrative contract (Q9c-014) and NCAF's 1-3-year Taiwan Top grants (Q9c-011, Q55-008).

Thu 19 Nov: twin of Q100-035 and the aha reserve Taiwan's founders had no year in hand (no registered fund held a year of running costs); adds public operators. This is absence of evidence, so never say no Taiwanese residency keeps a reserve.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e background, with Q9-031, Q9c-030 and Q140-036. Among the residencies found, closures came from the site, and no grant cut alone closed one. But founder-funded spaces closed when the founder's income stopped (Q100-014, Q100-030), so never say Taiwan's residencies die of losing the building, not money. About six cases.
